question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[X{Y}^{2}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}1,\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

current_example.problem:
Find $\textrm{E}\big[2X+Y\big],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154787/assets/d9783e551480eb63d81ebd48988f544df5eb01f3b4230771effbc036b7e86e7d.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\textrm{E}\big[r(X,Y)] = \iint_{\mathbb{R}^2} r(x,y) \, f(x,y) \: \textrm{d}x \textrm{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y) = 2x+y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonzero only in the rectangular region $D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1,\: 0 \leq y \leq 2 \right\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X+Y] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}(2x+y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+y)\cdot x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{2}+xy)\,\text{d}x\,]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}y}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{y}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\frac{2}{3}y+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
